builds.howItPlays: You play spells that give you extra runes, like Catalyst of Aeons, plus Platewyrm Egg, gear that adds energy and that Jayce can ready so it pays out twice a turn. Once Dazzling Aurora (9 cost) is out, at the end of each of your turns it reveals cards from the top of your deck until it hits a unit and plays that unit for free, and in this deck nearly every unit is Elder Dragon, a 12-cost unit with 10 Might.
builds.whyYou: You like a long game with one big goal: survive, build up, then let the card you worked toward do the rest. You don't mind having almost no units in the early turns, because your removal spells and card draw keep you alive until your expensive cards arrive. You enjoy counting the turns to Aurora and choosing when to spend Jayce's ability on your gear. If a free 10 Might dragon every turn sounds fun, this Jayce suits you.
builds.ratingNotes:
Change 2026-09-25. The Archetype stays Combo. Pace moves 3.5 to 1, Stance 5 to 3 and Complexity 7.5 to 7. Variance stays at 6. deckListUrl moves from the bare /decks page to the Best of Singapore RQ list. The old numbers came from reading two guides. The new ones are the mean of three scored decks from the picked style Dazzling Aurora Jayce (tools.ts style: Combo 1/3/7/6, labels Combo, Combo, Combo). riftboundguide.com's champion deck guide is dropped from guideUrls because it covers the older gear-combo framing, not this list.
Scored decks (pace/stance/complexity/variance):
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/80ef4860-8530-4d76-ac3c-060211e44477 Best of Singapore RQ (justmilkey), 1/3/7/6
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/b31f49fc-65be-4647-afce-d8793a46d3d6 Best of Barcelona RQ (Cramo), 1/3.5/7/5.5
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/11c926a0-8d34-4cf8-b760-970b17ad2d45 Best of Jayce, Auckland 10K (Thun), 1/3/7/6.5
Adjustments on all three: complexity +1 (the Legend readies gear such as Platewyrm Egg every turn and must be Empowered at the right time); pace -0.5 (Forgotten Monument delays scoring on one battlefield; on Cramo's list The Papertree also ramps both players).
Cards that decided each Axis:
- Pace: 4 units and none cheap, against 14 to 15 cards costing 5+ (Elder Dragon, Dazzling Aurora, Clairvoyance, Promising Future). The formula floors at 0 to 0.5 against a judged 2. That 2-point gap was re-read on every sheet and the tags stand.
- Stance: 7 to 9 answers (Bellows Breath, Flurry of Blades, Deadly Flourish, Rocket Barrage, Sabotage) against 2 to 3 pressure cards (Sprite Burst), inside a list of 28 to 31 own-plan cards.
- Complexity: 6 engine cards (Aurora, Elder Dragon), 10 to 12 cards that give extra runes (Mobilize, Catalyst of Aeons, Platewyrm Egg), and 15 to 16 card-flow cards (Clairvoyance, Dredge Up, Garbage Grabber).
- Variance: Promising Future's top-five play (luck, swing) and ramping into payoffs push it up. Heavy card flow pulls it back.
Legend ability: Empower for 2 energy plus 2 runes, once. 1 energy and exhaust: ready a gear. Once Empowered: ready 2 gear.
Also played: https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/e058b301-48f1-455e-a892-b9d7097cc799 (Mega Time Warp Ramp-Control, Poro Party TCG, Control 3/4/6/4.5) and https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/631f5d15-8770-4757-92ee-c20a1c30d5fd (Energy Jayce, squak, Control 2/4/6.5/5), from the Time Warp Ramp Jayce style: ramp into sweepers and Time Warp in place of Aurora.
Confidence: high.
Reviewer check: all three scored lists predate the 2026-09-18 ban, but that ban touches no card in them. riftbound.gg names cards only by code (OGN-160 and OGN-115 put UNL-118 into play for free). I read that as Aurora plus Promising Future into Elder Dragon, but did not confirm the codes.

builds.howItPlays: You fill the board with cheap units and gear, such as Patched Porobot (2 cost, draws a card if you control 3 other gear) and Sprite Fountain, which makes a 3 Might Sprite that lasts until your next turn. Jayce readies your gear, so Tools of Empire can give +2 Might twice in one turn, and Pit Crew readies itself each time you play a gear so it can fight again.
builds.whyYou: You like having units on the board from the first turns and fighting for a battlefield every turn. You enjoy the small puzzle of ordering your plays: which gear to play first so Pit Crew stands back up, which unit gets the boost from Tools of Empire, when to spend Jayce's ability. You'd rather win through lots of steady fights than one big payoff. If a busy board of small machines sounds fun, this Jayce suits you.

Adjustments on all three: complexity +1 (the Legend readies gear every turn, such as Tools of Empire twice or Orb of Regret and Platewyrm Egg on Senntis's list, so timing matters); stance +0.5 (the Legend readies Tools of Empire for extra pumps in fights). No Axis had a formula-judgment gap of 2 or more.
Cards that decided each Axis:
- Pace: 8 cheap units per 40 (Plundering Poro, Patched Porobot, Irresistible Faefolk), 15 to 21 units in all, and only 3 to 7 cards costing 5+.
- Stance: 17.5 to 24 pressure (Pit Crew, First Mate, Hwei, Sprite Fountain) against 6 to 9 answers (Challenge, Eclipse, Cloth Armor).
- Complexity: 16 to 21 setup or modes cards (First Mate, Pit Crew, Tools of Empire, Acceleration Gate) and 7 to 8 reactive cards.
- Variance: no luck or swing cards, and 53 to 75 percent of each list run as 3-ofs.
Legend ability: Empower for 2 energy plus 2 runes, once. 1 energy and exhaust: ready a gear. Once Empowered: ready 2 gear.
Also played: https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/01200e47-da91-445c-ba95-9bfd6970a035 (Combat Control - Full Guide, Rifeli, Midrange 5.5/6/7/4), from the Applied Researchers Kai'Sa Jayce style: cheap combat spells through Applied Researchers, replayed with Kai'Sa.
Confidence: high.
Reviewer check: the evidence behind this style is likes and guide pages, not tournament placings. Menda's and yourselvs's Piltover Archive guide sections read empty when fetched. All scored lists predate the 2026-09-18 ban, but that ban touches no card in them.
